summary: Slice-E XamPulse backend is approved. All eight checks pass: every new ClickHouse read (baselineSamples, processLatest, usageDailyBySource) goes through TenantScopedQueryBuilder.start() so the tenant_id IN (...) predicate and its ids are the first clause/params, and every user-influenced value (metric, instanceId, window bounds) is a bound parameter; the new write seam JdbcClickHouseWrites validates table and every column against a closed per-table whitelist before building SQL and binds all row values, chunked at 10k. Every new bean is @ConditionalOnProperty(xampulse.enabled=true) and xp-named (xpClickHouseWrites, xpEventWriter, xpBaselineJob, xpEc2StateEventProjection, xpUsageRollupJob, xpProcessQueryService, xpArchiveSearchController). The three scheduled jobs (BaselineJob, Ec2StateEventProjection, XpUsageRollupJob) return early unless isSchedulingEnabled() (and their enabled flag) and run each account in its own try/catch that swallows store errors by class name only. No shipped ClickHouse V001..V007 or shipped Flyway migrations were edited (only the new V008__writer_insert_grants.sql, an idempotent GRANT restatement). The Resource 360 series keys emitted by HostQueryService.summary() match Resource360Drawer.tsx exactly (system.cpu.utilization{state=steal|iowait}, {cpu=N}, system.paging.utilization, system.filesystem.utilization{mountpoint=/x}, system.disk.io{direction=read|write}, system.network.io{direction=receive|transmit}). Both new endpoints return the uniform 404 envelope for a foreign account via XamPulseAccessGuard.require / XamPulseException.notFound, and the archive-search route is estimate-only (running is DEFERRED) rejecting multi-account with XP_INVALID_REQUEST. No Beta Observability/OpenObserve code is touched. The unrelated GCP/Dockerfile/CI changes are left uncommitted in the working tree and are NOT part of the three XamPulse commits (c5f7880a5, 703a94dbc, 08a17f489), each of which contains only xampulse files. Unit tests exist for every new unit, and the full xampulse.** suite is green: 427 run, 0 failures, 0 errors; the pre-existing AwsPermissionCatalogKubernetesTest failure is outside this scope and was not introduced here. Only non-blocking LOW observations remain.

findings.detail: Per-core CPU keys are emitted as system.cpu.utilization{cpu=<raw cpu label>}, but the frontend coreSeries() only matches ^system\.cpu\.utilization\{cpu=(\d+)\}$ (digits only). If the OTel hostmetrics 'cpu' attribute ever arrives as a non-numeric string (e.g. 'cpu0'), the per-core chart silently renders nothing. FEAT-002 asserts OTel emits a numeric attribute, so this is a possible (not confirmed) edge and does not block. Likewise {state=iowait} is filtered literally; if the agent labels it 'wait' that one series is empty (graceful 'No data'), which is acceptable.
findings.fix: No change required for approval. Optionally add a contract/integration assertion that the agent's cpu-state label is 'iowait' and the cpu attribute is numeric, or normalise the label value when building the series key, so a labelling drift surfaces as a test failure rather than a blank chart.

findings.detail: The in-memory lastSeenHour dedupe map is unbounded per process lifetime (one entry per tenant|resource|state ever seen). Entries are only overwritten, never evicted, so a long-lived instance with many short-lived EC2 instance ids slowly grows the map. Bounded in practice by distinct EC2 ids per account and not a correctness or security issue; errors are swallowed and the primary ALERT/ANOMALY path is unaffected.
findings.fix: No change required for approval. Optionally cap or periodically prune the map (e.g. drop entries whose recorded hour is older than the current hour) if the EC2 fleet churn is high.
